title: CurvaDB: a certified curve store and a negative result on splines for trajectory storage
description:
Does storing GPS trajectories as cubic B-splines beat the classic Douglas-Peucker (DP) simplification, and can a curve store answer range queries over compressed trajectories with a provable guarantee on the true continuous Fréchet distance? Five results, four negative and one positive, all reached by fixing criteria before each run and measuring error against ground truth, never against a method's own observations:

  1. (Negative) A cubic B-spline is not a better compressor for real, consumer-grade GPS trajectories than a DP-simplified polyline: the DP polyline is smaller at every tested tolerance (3.7x smaller at tol=10 m).
  2. (Negative) Removing every confound (the spline's tethering to the polyline, the fitter's own weaknesses, noise, sampling sparsity via an oracle fit to the true curve) still doesn't save the spline: a decisive synthetic test's three pre-registered criteria all fail, and the oracle itself isn't more compact than DP+SED (292 vs. 278 bytes at tol=10 m).
  3. (Negative) The one gap that oracle left open — uniform knots only, not free/optimal placement — closes the same way: a certified, free-knot oracle fit directly on the true curve still doesn't beat DP+SED by the required 20% at any tested tolerance (closest: 0.834x at tol=2 m, against an 0.80x bar). This closes the project's open hypothesis on optimal knot placement.
  4. (Positive) A certified curve store can answer continuous-Fréchet range queries over compressed trajectories with a provable error bound, with zero misses and zero false positives across 6,000,000 tested combinations, and cheaper than an honest, uncompressed exact competitor (20.1 ms vs. 41.7 ms median per query).
  5. (Negative) That same store's spec-designated primary spline certificate mechanism doesn't work as designed (83.6% of splines fall back to the secondary path, against a required ≤10%), and the correctness guarantee has a real, measured price against an uncertified approximate search (2.7x–4.4x slower).

Methodology throughout: criteria fixed before each run (never adjusted afterward to fit the data), an oracle fit to ground truth to separate a representation's own limits from a specific fitter's, error measured against ground truth rather than a method's own noisy observations, and a negative result treated as a normal, reportable outcome.

Full technical report: docs/REPORT.md. Raw results per step: benchmarks/results/. Full decision history (23 architecture decision records): docs/decisions/.
